rows.title: Lamont wants lawmakers to keep CT budget guardrails in place
rows.standfirst: CT’s strong financial situation has led to to calls for tax cuts or more spending or both. Gov. Lamont wants to keep the safeguards in place.

rows.title: CT government can spend more as inflation soars. But should it?
rows.standfirst: CT legislators are eyeing more funds for child care, municipal aid and education as inflation has increased how much the state can spend.

rows.title: Sema4 settles up with CT after relocating labs out of the state
rows.standfirst: Sema4, now known as GeneDx, has paid back $2 million of a $15.5M state loan and agreed to a reduction in how much the state would forgive.

rows.title: Even with gas tax holiday, CT’s transportation coffers are flush
rows.standfirst: CT Republicans want tax cuts, but labor and business say the sluggish highway building program threatens the state’s economic future.

rows.title: CT tax receipts surge as Lamont prepares new tax-cutting plan
rows.standfirst: Projections for state tax receipts increased again, pushing the current fiscal year’s surplus beyond $3 billion, according to a new report.

rows.title: CT Port Authority is likely to ask for more money for State Pier
rows.standfirst: Last year, CT Port Authority promised that taxpayers would not need to contribute any more money to the New London State Pier redevelopment.

rows.title: Lamont proposes tax cut for small and mid-sized businesses
rows.standfirst: Lamont will propose to cut the pass-through entity tax as part of the budget plan he will deliver to the General Assembly on Feb. 8.

rows.title: New CT state police contract offers raises to boost recruitment
rows.standfirst: A new contract could boost wages for CT state police nearly 10% in its first year as Connecticut tries to reverse a recruitment crisis.

rows.title: CT nonprofits want $482 million funding boost
rows.standfirst: CT social service providers, after years of underfunding, have sights set on the budget surplus to fix understaffing and other issues.

rows.title: Connecticut’s gas tax is returning incrementally. What’s going on?
rows.standfirst: CT’s 25-cents-per-gallon gas tax was suspended in March 2022 due to rising fuel prices. As of Jan. 1, the state is gradually restoring it.

rows.title: CT essential worker relief payments will be issued starting Feb. 1
rows.standfirst: CT will begin issuing pandemic bonuses to private-sector workers on Feb. 1. More than 150,000 essential workers will receive payments.

rows.title: CT tax cuts are likely, but fierce debate expected over who benefits
rows.standfirst: CT’s fiscally moderate Democratic Gov. Ned Lamont may find more allies among Republicans when it comes to proposals to cut taxes.

rows.title: Democrats to Lamont: Ease fiscal restraints for CT schools’ sake
rows.standfirst: Lamont wants to keep fiscal ‘guardrails’ in place, but legislators see a way to increase education funding with savings from the revenue cap.

rows.title: LIHEAP can help CT families cover energy costs. How is it funded and who qualifies?
rows.standfirst: LIHEAP helps low-income families pay for winter heating and other energy costs. Here’s an overview of the program and its eligibility requirements.

rows.title: Lamont unveils $45M tax cut for CT’s working poor
rows.standfirst: The expanded earned income tax credit would save families about $211 per year on average and make CT’s EITC rate among the highest.
